dedupe_keys.name: east bronx shared e scooter pilot evaluation nyc dot 2022

description: This is the legally required evaluation, by New York City's Department of Transportation (NYC DOT), of the East Bronx shared electric scooter pilot mandated by Local Law 74 of 2020. The pilot tested shared e-scooters in neighbourhoods not served by Citi Bike, with three operators, Bird, Lime and Veo. Phase 1 launched on 17 August 2021 with up to 3,000 scooters; Phase 2 followed on 22 June 2022, with up to 6,000 scooters across both phases. Coverage: the first year of trips (17 August 2021 to 31 August 2022), shared by the operators in Mobility Data Specification format without personal data, plus 1,696 rider and non-rider survey responses, field inspections and outreach. Over 86,000 rider accounts made more than a million trips, about 2,800 a day, with more trips on weekdays and in warm months; popular routes linked to subway stations and bus and ferry stops, and no fatalities were reported. The report covers mobility, safety, operations and data, parking, equity and accessible scooters. Format and access: a 38-page PDF report. Licence and cost: free to read; no licence is stated. Caveats: operator data quality and GPS accuracy limited some analyses. The ridership and fleet figures can be used to calibrate micromobility demand in agent-based or network flow models of first and last mile access. It relates to the Mobility Data Specification, Citi Bike data and the FOMOsim simulator in the catalogue.
